All East Bay Properties is a full-service real estate brokerage and property management company serving Alameda and Contra Costa Counties since 2005. With over 20 years of continuous operation and 600+ residential properties under active management throughout the East Bay.
We leverage AppFolio property management software to deliver transparent, efficient service through dedicated tenant and owner portals with mobile access. We also provide advanced AI leasing assistance using AppFolio's LISA for initial prospect management and showing scheduling.

Our portfolio includes properties in premier East Bay communities such as Bridgewater, Watergate, Pacific Park Plaza, The Terraces, Andante, Bay Street, Elevation 22, City Limits, Emeryville Warehouse (1500 Park), Green City Lofts and Emery Bay Village.

## Common Questions

**Q: What is the Oakland allowable rent increase for 2026?**
A: 2.3%, effective August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027. The Oakland Rent Adjustment Program (RAP) sets this rate at 60% of CPI (capped at 3%). This applies to rent-stabilized units under the Oakland Rent Adjustment Ordinance (O.M.C. 8.22.020 et seq.). It does not apply to units exempt from Oakland rent stabilization or to AB 1482-only units (which use a separate CPI-based calculation). The prior period (August 1, 2025 – July 31, 2026) was 0.8%.

**Q: What is the Berkeley allowable rent increase for 2026?**
A: 1.0%. The Berkeley Rent Board set the 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) at 1.0%, effective January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026. Berkeley runs on a calendar-year cycle (not the August–July cycle used by Oakland and AB 1482) and uses a different CPI region and lookback window. Applies to Berkeley rent-stabilized units under the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance (BMC Chapter 13.76).

**Q: What is the Richmond allowable rent increase for 2026?**
A: 1.5%, for tenancies commencing before September 1, 2025, effective September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 (Richmond Rent Program Regulation 615). The rate is 60% of CPI, capped at 3%, post-Measure P. Banked (deferred) increases allow up to 6.5% in a single year, per Regulation 602's banking limit.

**Q: What is the statewide AB 1482 rent cap for 2026?**
A: 8.8%, effective August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027 (5% + regional CPI, under Civil Code §1947.12's 10% hard cap). This applies statewide for units covered by Civil Code §1947.12, including Alameda and Contra Costa Counties. AB 1482 has its own statutory exemptions, so exemption from a local rent-control program does not automatically establish AB 1482 coverage. Oakland, Berkeley, and Richmond also impose separate local limits on units covered by their respective programs. The prior period (August 1, 2025 – July 31, 2026) was 6.3%.

**Q: What is the Oakland nonpayment eviction threshold?**
A: Under Oakland's Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (OMC 8.22.360), a nonpayment eviction notice is only valid if the tenant's unpaid balance equals or exceeds one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size in the Oakland-Fremont metro area — not the tenant's actual contract rent. FY 2027 FMR thresholds (effective October 1, 2026): Studio $2,088 | 1BR $2,290 | 2BR $2,805 | 3BR $3,592 | 4BR $4,250. Through September 30, 2026 (FY 2026): Studio $2,142 | 1BR $2,385 | 2BR $2,912 | 3BR $3,724 | 4BR $4,413.

**Q: Does Oakland just cause eviction apply to single-family homes?**
A: Yes, as of Measure V (November 2022). Most Oakland rental units are covered, including single-family homes, condos, ADUs, and RVs built more than 10 years ago. Key exemptions: units where the owner shares a kitchen or bathroom with the tenant; units with a Certificate of Occupancy issued within the last 10 years (rolling window).

**Q: What is AB 1482?**
A: California's Tenant Protection Act of 2019. Statewide law that caps annual rent increases at 5% + local CPI (max 10%) for covered units, and requires just cause for eviction after 12 months of tenancy. Oakland and Berkeley local ordinances are stricter and take precedence for most units in those cities.

**Q: What is the California security deposit limit?**
A: As of July 1, 2024 (AB 12), California landlords may collect a maximum of one month's rent as a security deposit, regardless of whether the unit is furnished. Prior law allowed two months (unfurnished) or three months (furnished). Small landlord exemptions apply in limited circumstances.

**Q: How do I contact All East Bay Properties?**
A: Main office: 510-450-3800. Email: web@alleastbayproperties.com. Address: 2324 Powell St., Emeryville, CA 94608. Hours: Monday–Friday 10am–3pm or by appointment. 24/7 maintenance: 510-450-3815.

## HUD Fair Market Rents & Income Limits

**Area:** Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR Area
**Effective:** October 1, 2026 (FY 2027). Updates annually each October.
**Source:** HUD USER — https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html

### FY 2027 Fair Market Rents — Oakland-Fremont Metro

| Unit Size     | FY 2027 FMR (from Oct 1, 2026) | FY 2026 FMR (through Sep 30, 2026) |
|---------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Efficiency    | $2,088                         | $2,142                             |
| 1-Bedroom     | $2,290                         | $2,385                             |
| 2-Bedroom     | $2,805                         | $2,912                             |
| 3-Bedroom     | $3,592                         | $3,724                             |
| 4-Bedroom     | $4,250                         | $4,413                             |

**Primary use for East Bay landlords:** Oakland's Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (OMC 8.22.360) requires that unpaid rent equal or exceed one month's HUD FMR for the unit's bedroom size before a nonpayment eviction notice is legally valid. The threshold is based on FMR — not the tenant's actual contract rent. A tenant paying $1,400/month on a 1-bedroom must owe at least $2,290 (from October 1, 2026) before a valid notice can be served. See: https://alleastbayproperties.com/oakland-just-cause-eviction-grounds-2026/

FMR figures are also used as payment standards for Section 8 / Housing Choice Voucher participants in the Oakland metro.

**Area Median Family Income (MFI):** $162,800

| Income Category         | 1-Person | 2-Person | 3-Person | 4-Person | 5-Person | 6-Person | 7-Person  | 8-Person  |
|-------------------------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Extremely Low (30% AMI) | $35,650  | $40,750  | $45,850  | $50,900  | $55,000  | $59,050  | $63,150   | $67,200   |
| Very Low (50% AMI)      | $59,400  | $67,900  | $76,400  | $84,850  | $91,650  | $98,450  | $105,250  | $112,050  |
| Low (80% AMI)           | $95,050  | $108,600 | $122,200 | $135,750 | $146,650 | $157,500 | $168,350  | $179,200  |

**Note:** Income limits are used to determine eligibility for HUD-assisted housing programs including Section 8 / Housing Choice Voucher. They are not directly used in Oakland's rent control or just-cause eviction frameworks but provide context for assessing housing affordability in the East Bay rental market.

**Data currency note:** Fair Market Rents update each October; this file shows FY 2027 FMRs (effective October 1, 2026). The income limits above are the FY 2026 figures; HUD publishes new income limits each spring.

## California Rental Law Library

One page per law affecting East Bay residential landlords (California, Alameda and Contra Costa Counties, Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville, Richmond). Each page shows its status, effective date, key figures, official source and the date it was last checked.
Library: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/
Machine-readable: https://alleastbayproperties.com/llms-laws.json
Most recent review: 2026-10-14

### 3-Day Notices in California: Pay or Quit, Cure or Quit, and How to Serve Them
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/three-day-notices-and-service/
California | In force | Code Civ. Proc. §§ 1161, 1162 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Before an eviction for unpaid rent or a lease breach, California requires a written 3-day notice that excludes weekends and court holidays, contains specific payment details, and is served by one of three approved methods.
Key figures: Notice period: 3 days, excluding weekends and court holidays; Time to serve a rent notice: Within 1 year after rent was due; Payment bank location: Within 5 miles of the property; Fee for serving a notice: Not allowed

### AB 1482 Just Cause: When a California Landlord Can End a Tenancy
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-1482-just-cause/
California | In force | AB 1482 (Tenant Protection Act); Civ. Code § 1946.2 | Effective 2020-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: After a tenant has lived in a covered California rental for 12 months, the owner can end the tenancy only for a listed at-fault or no-fault reason, stated in the notice. No-fault endings require one month's rent in relocation help.
Key figures: Occupancy before protection starts: 12 months (24 in some added-tenant cases); No-fault relocation: One month's rent, paid within 15 days, or final month waived; Owner move-in: occupant must move in: Within 90 days and stay 12 months; Substantial remodel threshold: Permitted work requiring the tenant out 30+ days

### AB 1482 Rent Cap: California’s Statewide Limit on Rent Increases
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-1482-rent-cap/
California | In force | AB 1482 (Tenant Protection Act); Civ. Code § 1947.12 | Effective 2020-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Most California rentals over 15 years old can't be raised more than 5% plus local CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12 months. In the East Bay that cap is 8.8% from August 1, 2026.
Key figures: East Bay cap (Aug 1, 2026 to Jul 31, 2027): 8.8% (5% + 3.8% CPI); Previous period (Aug 1, 2025 to Jul 31, 2026): 6.3% (5% + 1.3% CPI); Absolute maximum: 10% in any 12 months; CPI used: San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward CPI-U, April to April

### AB 2025: Disclosing Digitally Altered Photos in Rental Ads
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-2025-altered-rental-listing-photos/
California | Upcoming | AB 2025 (Stats. 2026); Civ. Code § 1940.11 (new); Bus. & Prof. Code § 10140.8 | Effective 2027-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-29
Summary: Starting January 1, 2027, California rental ads that use AI-generated or digitally altered photos must say so on or next to the image and include, or link to, the original unaltered photo.
Key figures: Effective date: January 1, 2027; Disclosure placement: On or next to each altered image, reasonably conspicuous; Original photo: In the posting, or via link, URL, or QR code; Lease length covered: Rental ads of any lease length

### AB 2347: 10 Court Days to Answer an Eviction Lawsuit
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-2347-eviction-answer-period/
California | In force | AB 2347 (Stats. 2024, ch. 512); CCP §§ 1167, 1170 | Effective 2025-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Since January 1, 2025, a California tenant served with an eviction complaint has 10 court days to respond, up from 5, plus 5 more court days if served by mail. Demurrers are heard 5 to 7 court days after filing.
Key figures: Response time: 10 court days, excluding weekends and court holidays; Added for service by mail: 5 court days; Demurrer or motion to strike hearing: 5 to 7 court days after filing; Effective: January 1, 2025

### AB 246: Social Security Hardship Defense in Nonpayment Evictions
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-246-social-security-eviction-defense/
California | In force | AB 246 (Stats. 2025, ch. 337); Civ. Code § 1946.3 | Effective 2026-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-10-14
Summary: Until January 20, 2029, a California tenant sued for unpaid rent can ask the court to pause the eviction if a federal interruption in Social Security benefits caused the nonpayment. The rent is still owed once benefits resume.
Key figures: Effective: January 1, 2026; Length of stay: Until 14 days after benefits are restored, or 6 months, whichever is earlier; Tenant deadline after benefits resume: 14 days to pay all past-due rent or agree to a payment plan; Cases covered: Nonpayment of rent only

### AB 2801: Security Deposit Photos
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-2801-security-deposit-photos/
California | In force | AB 2801 (Stats. 2024, ch. 280); Civ. Code § 1950.5 | Effective 2025-04-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Landlords must photograph a unit at move-out before cleaning or repairs, again after that work, and at move-in for tenancies starting July 1, 2025 or later, then send the photos with the deposit statement.
Key figures: Deposit return and itemized statement deadline: 21 calendar days after move-out; Move-out and after-repair photos: Required since Apr 1, 2025; Move-in photos: Tenancies starting on or after Jul 1, 2025; Bad-faith retention: Up to 2x the deposit, plus actual damages

### AB 747 (SPARE Act): Stricter Proof of Service in Evictions
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ab-747-spare-act-service-of-process/
California | Upcoming | AB 747 (Stats. 2025, ch. 563), as amended by AB 2042 (Stats. 2026, ch. 379); Code Civ. Proc. §§ 415.20, 415.45, 417.10, 473.2, 1166 | Effective 2027-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-29
Summary: Starting January 1, 2027, eviction complaints must state when, where, and how the termination notice was served, and process servers must document service with timestamped, GPS-tagged photos after three real attempts.
Key figures: Operative date: January 1, 2027; Attempts before substituted service or posting: 3, on 3 different days at 3 different times; Photo stamp on proof of service: Date, time, and GPS coordinates

### Berkeley Owner Move-In and Ellis Act Relocation Payments
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/berkeley-omi-ellis-relocation/
Berkeley | In force | Berkeley Municipal Code §§ 13.76.130(A)(8), 13.77.055 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Berkeley owners who recover a unit for owner move-in or withdraw it under the Ellis Act must pay $19,413 per household in 2026, plus $6,471 for qualifying households, deposited in escrow with the City.
Key figures: Standard relocation (2026): $19,413; Additional payment (2026): $6,471 for low-income, disabled, elderly (60+), minor children, or pre-1999 tenancies; Owner move-in escrow deposit: Within 10 days of serving the notice; Unpaid relocation: 3x the payment plus attorney's fees

### Berkeley Rent Registration, Fees, and Security Deposit Interest
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/berkeley-registration-fees-deposit-interest/
Berkeley | In force | Berkeley Municipal Code §§ 13.76.070, 13.76.080, 13.76.110(E) | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Berkeley landlords must register covered units, re-register within 15 days of each new tenancy, pay the annual registration fee by July 1, and pay tenants interest on security deposits every year.
Key figures: Annual registration fee due: July 1; Late fee penalty: 100% of the fee, increasing every 6 months unpaid; New-tenancy notice and re-registration: Within 15 days; Deposit interest year: Nov 1 to Oct 31; paid each December, no later than Jan 31

### Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Ordinance
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/berkeley-rent-stabilization-just-cause/
Berkeley | In force | Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance; Measure BB) | Effective 2026-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Berkeley limits yearly increases on most older units to its Annual General Adjustment, 1.0% for 2026, and requires just cause to end any covered tenancy from day one, with notices filed at the Rent Board.
Key figures: 2026 Annual General Adjustment: 1.0% (Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026); How the AGA is set: 65% of the SF-Oakland-San Jose CPI change (year to June 30), between 0% and 5%; New tenancy first eligible for AGA: Second January after move-in (e.g., Mar 2026 move-in: Jan 2028); File eviction notices with Rent Board: Within 3 business days of service

### California Fair Housing: Protected Classes and Source of Income
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/california-fair-housing-source-of-income/
California | In force | Gov. Code §§ 12927, 12955 (FEHA); SB 329 (2019); SB 267 (2023); SB 1137 and AB 1815 (2024) | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: California's fair housing law bars rental discrimination on 16 grounds, including source of income, so landlords can't refuse Section 8 or other subsidies and must judge income only on the tenant's share of the rent.
Key figures: Protected classes (Gov. Code 12955): 16, plus perceived traits and association; Housing vouchers: Count as source of income, including Section 8 and HUD-VASH, since Jan 1, 2020; Subsidized applicants: Income test on the tenant's share of rent only; Credit history alternative: Required for subsidized applicants since Jan 1, 2024

### Costa-Hawkins: Limits on Local Rent Control
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/costa-hawkins-rental-housing-act/
California | In force | Civ. Code §§ 1954.50–1954.535 | Effective 1996-01-01 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Costa-Hawkins lets owners set rents freely on units first certified for occupancy after February 1, 1995 and on most single-family homes and condos, and lets them reset rent between tenancies under local rent control.
Key figures: New-construction exemption: Certificate of occupancy after Feb 1, 1995, or an earlier local exemption; Oakland rent control cutoff: Applies to units built before January 1, 1983; Ending a Section 8 contract: 90 days' notice to the tenant; Code-violation bar: Cited, unabated 60+ days before the vacancy

### Emeryville Just Cause, Relocation, and Business License Rules
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/emeryville-just-cause-relocation/
Emeryville | In force | Emeryville Municipal Code Title 5, Ch. 40 (§§ 5-40.01–5-40.08) | Effective 2017-04-01 | Last reviewed 2026-10-02
Summary: Emeryville has no rent control, but landlords need a valid business license and a listed cause to end any tenancy, must use the city's notice form, file it with the City Clerk, and pay relocation for no-fault endings.
Key figures: Relocation, large landlord (5+ units in Emeryville): Greater of 5x HUD Fair Market Rent or 4x current rent; Relocation, small landlord (4 or fewer units): Greater of 1x HUD Fair Market Rent or 1 month's rent; Example: large landlord, 1BR from Oct 1, 2026: At least $11,450 (5 x $2,290); Copy of notice to City Clerk: Within 10 days of delivery

### Ending a Month-to-Month Tenancy: 30- and 60-Day Notices
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/ending-month-to-month-tenancy-notice/
California | In force | Civ. Code §§ 1946, 1946.1 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Where just cause doesn't apply, a California landlord ends a month-to-month tenancy with 60 days' written notice, or 30 days if the tenant has lived there less than a year, using required notice language.
Key figures: Tenant there 1 year or more: 60 days' written notice; Tenant there less than 1 year: 30 days' written notice; Sale to an owner-occupant buyer: 30 days, within 120 days of opening escrow; Notice service fee: Can't be charged to the tenant

### Habitability: What a California Landlord Must Maintain
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/habitability-repairs-california/
California | In force | Civ. Code §§ 1941, 1941.1, 1942 (as amended by AB 628) | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: California landlords must keep rentals fit to live in, meeting a statutory list that now includes a working stove and refrigerator. If a landlord doesn't repair within a reasonable time, tenants can repair and deduct up to one month's rent.
Key figures: Stove and refrigerator required: Leases entered into, amended, or extended on or after Jan 1, 2026; Recalled appliance: Repair or replace within 30 days of notice; Repair-and-deduct limit: Up to one month's rent, twice in 12 months; Presumed reasonable repair time: 30 days after notice

### Landlord Entry: Notice and Access Rules (Civil Code 1954)
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/civil-code-1954-landlord-entry/
California | In force | Civ. Code § 1954; § 1940.2(a)(4), (b) | Last reviewed 2026-10-14
Summary: A California landlord may enter a rental only for listed reasons, such as repairs, showings, emergencies or a court order, and usually only during normal business hours after reasonable written notice, presumed to be 24 hours.
Key figures: Written notice presumed reasonable: 24 hours; Mailed notice presumed reasonable: Mailed at least 6 days before entry; Oral notice for buyer showings: Allowed if written for-sale notice was given within 120 days; Orally agreed repair entry: Within 1 week of the agreement

### Oakland Business Tax Certificate for Rental Property
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-business-tax-certificate-rentals/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code ch. 5.04 (§§ 5.04.205, 5.04.300, 5.04.400); O.M.C. §§ 8.22.070, 8.22.090, 8.22.360 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Oakland taxes rental income at $13.95 per $1,000 of gross receipts, due March 1, and a current Business Tax Certificate is required to raise rent, take part in a RAP petition, or serve owner move-in and repair evictions.
Key figures: Tax rate (Class O rentals): $13.95 per $1,000 of gross receipts; Annual due date: March 1; Late penalty: 10% at the deadline, plus 25% after 60 days, plus 1% a month interest; New rental registration: Within 30 days of starting

### Oakland Fair Chance Housing Ordinance: Criminal History in Screening
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-fair-chance-housing/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code ch. 8.25 (Ord. No. 13581) | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Oakland bars most landlords from asking about, requiring disclosure of, or acting on an applicant's criminal history, with narrow exceptions for screening required by state or federal law and the lifetime sex offender registry.
Key figures: City civil penalty: Up to $1,000 per violation; Damages in a lawsuit: 3x the greater of actual damages, one month's rent, or the HUD Small Area FMR; Records retention: Keep any criminal history obtained for at least 3 years; Adopted: February 4, 2020

### Oakland Just Cause for Eviction (Measure EE)
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-just-cause-eviction/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code ch. 8.22, Art. II (§§ 8.22.300–8.22.390) | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Oakland landlords can end most tenancies only for one of the ordinance's listed causes, with specific notice language, a copy filed with the Rent Board within 10 days, and a current rent registration.
Key figures: Nonpayment threshold from Oct 1, 2026: studio / 1BR: $2,088 / $2,290 (HUD FY 2027 FMR); Nonpayment threshold from Oct 1, 2026: 2BR / 3BR / 4BR: $2,805 / $3,592 / $4,250 (HUD FY 2027 FMR); Through Sep 30, 2026 (FY 2026): 1BR / 2BR: $2,385 / $2,912; File notice with Rent Board: Within 10 days of service

### Oakland RAP Fee and Rent Registry
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-rap-fee-and-rent-registry/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code §§ 8.22.500–8.22.520 (Art. IV) | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Oakland charges an annual Rent Program Service Fee on units covered by rent control or just cause, due January 1, and requires those units to be registered in the Rent Registry by March 1 each year.
Key figures: RAP fee per unit: $137 (as of Jul 1, 2025); Tenant pass-through (if paid on time): Half the fee ($68.50); Fee due / delinquent: Jan 1 / after Mar 1; Rent Registry deadline: March 1 each year

### Oakland Relocation Payments for No-Fault Evictions
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-relocation-payments/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code §§ 8.22.800–8.22.870 (Arts. VII and VIII) | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Oakland owners must pay relocation to tenants displaced by a no-fault eviction: $8,293 to $12,599 per unit from July 1, 2026, plus $2,500 for qualifying households, with owner move-in payments prorated by length of tenancy.
Key figures: Studio or 1 bedroom: $8,293.13 per unit; 2 bedrooms: $10,206.93 per unit; 3 or more bedrooms: $12,599.18 per unit; Additional payment: $2,500 per unit for lower-income, elderly (62+), or disabled tenants or minor children

### Oakland Rent Adjustment Program (RAP): Allowable Rent Increases
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-rent-adjustment-program/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code ch. 8.22, Art. I (Rent Adjustment Ordinance) | Effective 2026-08-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Rent increases on most Oakland units in buildings from before 1983 are capped at the city's allowable annual increase, and every increase notice must include the City's RAP Notice.
Key figures: Allowable annual increase (Aug 1, 2026 to Jul 31, 2027): 2.3%; Previous period (Aug 1, 2025 to Jul 31, 2026): 0.8%; How the rate is set: 60% of the April-to-April CPI change, or 3%, whichever is lower; Increase that includes banked amounts: Up to 3x the current allowable increase (6.9% this period)

### Oakland Tenant Protection Ordinance (Anti-Harassment)
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/oakland-tenant-protection-ordinance/
Oakland | In force | Oakland Municipal Code §§ 8.22.600–8.22.680 (Art. V) | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Oakland's Tenant Protection Ordinance bars bad-faith harassment of tenants, caps late fees at 3% of rent, limits removing parking or storage, and requires owners to give every tenant a TPO notice.
Key figures: Late fee cap: 3% of monthly rent, only after rent is 5+ days late (leases from Apr 16, 2020); Repeat buyout offers: No more than once in 6 months after a written request to stop; Minimum tenant damages: $1,000 per violation, $2,000 elderly or disabled, $2,500 catastrophically ill, or 3x actual; Time to sue: 3 years

### Rent Increase Notice Rules: 30 or 90 Days (Civil Code 827)
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/rent-increase-notice-civil-code-827/
California | In force | Civ. Code § 827 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: A California rent increase of 10% or less needs at least 30 days' written notice; above 10%, counting all increases in the past 12 months, it needs 90 days. Mailed notices need extra time.
Key figures: Increase of 10% or less: 30 days' notice; Increase over 10% (12-month total): 90 days' notice; Delivery: Personal delivery or mail (plus CCP 1013 mailing time)

### Richmond Fair Rent, Just Cause for Eviction and Homeowner Protection Ordinance
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/richmond-fair-rent-just-cause/
Richmond | In force | Richmond Municipal Code ch. 11.100 (Measure L) | Effective 2026-09-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: Richmond limits increases on older multi-unit rentals to its Annual General Adjustment, 1.5% from September 1, 2026, requires one of eight just causes to end a tenancy, and requires notices to be filed with the Rent Program.
Key figures: Annual General Adjustment (Sep 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027): 1.5% (approved June 17, 2026); Previous period (Sep 1, 2025 to Aug 31, 2026): 1.62%; Maximum with banked increases: Up to 6.5%; How the AGA is set: 60% of the SF-Oakland-San Jose CPI change (year to March), max 3%, never below 0

### SB 1296: Written Pet Policies Before Rental Applications
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/sb-1296-pet-policy-disclosure/
California | Upcoming | SB 1296 (Stats. 2026, ch. 1025); Civ. Code § 1942.7.5 (new) | Effective 2027-04-01 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Starting April 1, 2027, California landlords must have a written pet policy, even a no-pets policy, link it in online listings, and give it with every rental application, or refund the application fee on request.
Key figures: Operative date: April 1, 2027; Application fee refund: Within 7 business days of a written request; Where to link the policy: Property website, digital ads, and rental search listings, where the platform allows; No-pets properties: Still need a written policy

### SB 567: Owner Move-In and Substantial Remodel Evictions
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/sb-567-owner-move-in-remodel/
California | In force | SB 567 (Stats. 2023, ch. 290); Civ. Code § 1946.2(b)(2)(A), (D), (h) | Effective 2024-04-01 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: Under SB 567, an AB 1482 owner move-in requires the owner or relative to move in within 90 days and stay 12 months, and a substantial remodel requires permitted work that keeps the tenant out 30+ days.
Key figures: Move-in deadline: Within 90 days after the tenant leaves; Required occupancy: 12 consecutive months as a primary residence; Remodel threshold: Tenant must be out at least 30 consecutive days; Willful violation: Up to 3x actual damages, plus punitive damages

### Security Deposits: The One-Month Cap and 21-Day Return Rule
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/security-deposit-cap-and-return/
California | In force | Civ. Code § 1950.5 (as amended by AB 12, AB 2801, AB 414) | Effective 2024-07-01 | Last reviewed 2026-09-25
Summary: California caps most security deposits at one month's rent, furnished or not, and requires the balance plus an itemized statement within 21 days after the tenant moves out.
Key figures: Deposit cap: One month's rent, furnished or unfurnished; Small-landlord exception: Two months if a natural person or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than 2 properties with 4 or fewer units total; Return deadline: 21 calendar days after move-out; Bad-faith retention: Up to 2x the deposit, plus actual damages

### Self-Help Eviction, Harassment, and Retaliation in California
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/self-help-eviction-harassment-retaliation/
California | In force | Civ. Code §§ 789.3, 1940.2, 1942.5 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: California landlords can't lock out a tenant, shut off utilities, remove belongings, or harass a tenant into leaving, and can't evict, raise rent, or cut services in retaliation for a habitability complaint.
Key figures: Lockout or utility shutoff: Up to $100 a day, at least $250 per cause of action, plus actual damages; Harassment to force a move-out: Civil penalty up to $2,000 per violation; Retaliation window: 180 days after a habitability complaint, inspection, or case; Retaliation punitive damages: $100 to $2,000 per act, for fraud, oppression, or malice

### Unincorporated Alameda County Just Cause for Eviction
URL: https://alleastbayproperties.com/california-rental-laws/alameda-county-unincorporated-just-cause/
Alameda County | In force | Alameda County Ordinance Code ch. 3.70 (Ord. No. O-2025-9) | Effective 2025-03-06 | Last reviewed 2026-10-05
Summary: In unincorporated Alameda County, landlords need an AB 1482 just cause to end most tenancies after 12 months, must pay two months' rent (up to $10,000) for no-fault endings, and must file notices with the County within 3 days.
Key figures: No-fault relocation: 2 months' rent, capped at $10,000 per household; Notice filing with the County: Within 3 days of service; No-fault notice to vulnerable households: At least 90 days; Right of return after move-in or remodel: 1 year

### How to Stop Package Theft in an Apartment Building: What Actually Works in Older East Bay Buildings
